posts.topic_title: H2 DCG from Tony's H1 silvers.
posts.author: JohnFP
posts.post_subject: H2 DCG from Tony's H1 silvers.
posts.content_md:
Well, I have been working on a copy from some masters I got from Tony. Bless him, I have had them since the begining of the summer. First my laser died, then I had a few other problems. Well I had a few plates left over from Friday night and I finally got my table set up for an H1 to H2 copy so I decided to try what I had. The holograms are really clear, crystal clear, and bright but not as bright as I should be able to get them with fresher film. Not only that but I used the good plates up and these were the last two of the 6 that were left overs. You can see the boo-boos in coating. 

Here is the first one. All the funky going on with the black is the background through the hologram as you can see two other holograms behind this one showing up at the bottom. 4x5 mater into a 5x7 DCG.

![Image](http://www.holograms3d.com/PhotoGal/SeaHorse/SeaHorse1.JPG)

And the second one. 4x5 master into a 5x7 DCG.

![Image](http://www.holograms3d.com/PhotoGal/SeaHorse/SeaHorse2.JPG)

Thanks Tony and I have off this friday and hope to put in a good session with your masters. Table is reconfigured and ready to go.

John

The Seahorses - Finally a floor (the floor is clearer in real life).

![Image](http://www.holograms3d.com/PhotoGal/SeaHorse/TonySeaHorse.jpg)

The Dragon - Excellently bright. My wife said the hologram looks like it is made out of gold with diamond chips on it. Again, in real life virtually no blurryness.

![Image](http://www.holograms3d.com/PhotoGal/SeaHorse/TonyDragon.jpg)

posts.topic_title: H2 DCG from Tony's H1 silvers.
posts.author: Tony
posts.post_subject: H2 DCG from Tony's H1 silvers.
posts.content_md:
The masters are split beam transmission H1's, using a (semi-) collimated overhead reference beam. 35mW Hene laser, 4x5" BB-640, JD-4 developer, Fe EDTA bleach.

Thanks for the kind words!

posts.topic_title: H2 DCG from Tony's H1 silvers.
posts.author: JohnFP
posts.post_subject: H2 DCG from Tony's H1 silvers.
posts.content_md:
The recoding geometry is pretty much the same as the way I did Michael's elephant. I don't have a decent BS so I don't use one.

5x7 DCG. Plates were 4 1/2 (seahorses) and 5 hours (dragon) old. Emulsion facing object.

Exiting the spatial filter, the blue lines are the reference beam and the red lines are the object beam. The flat and concave mirrors are mounted over one another.

![Image](http://www.holograms3d.com/PhotoGal/MichHolo/IMG_2764.JPG)

posts.content_md:
As per a conversation with Dave.

Here is the same set up but with the configuration of having the H1 masteing set up built in. This configuration allows an H1 mastering and an H1 to H2 without changing anything, just blockdifferent parts of the beam exiting the spatial filter. For mastering cover the upper left mirror and for H1 to H2 cover the two mirrors on the plateholder and object.

![Image](http://www.holograms3d.com/Illustrations/H1H2NoBeamSplitter.jpg)
